additional_sources.best_for: National park guide
additional_sources.recommendation: A full park guide: best time to visit is July–September. Sights include Lake Clark itself, Proenneke Cabin at Twin Lakes, Turquoise Lake, Port Alsworth, Chinitna Bay, Crescent Lake, Redoubt and Iliamna volcanoes, and Telaquana Lake; top hikes are Beaver Pond Loop (3.5 mi easy), Teetering Rock (1.8), Tanalian Falls (4.3), Kontrashibuna Lake (4.3) and Tanalian Mountain (9.6 hard). The guide's key tip: the park has no road access — arrive by air taxi or floatplane from Anchorage or Homer, and build in buffer days because pass weather can ground bush planes.

additional_sources.best_for: National park / Their favorite way to visit Katmai
additional_sources.recommendation: Kelley & Carl's favorite way to visit Katmai: reserve Brooks Camp camping permits in January/February on recreation.gov, fly Alaska Airlines from Anchorage to King Salmon, then float plane with Katmai Air to Brooks Camp. Day trips work too, but the viewing platforms get crowded for hours at midday — camping lets you watch the bears in the quiet hours. July is the classic month.
additional_sources.source_title: How to visit Katmai for the bears

additional_sources.best_for: National park / 'For all the bear lovers'
additional_sources.recommendation: Kelley & Carl's Katmai guide: every summer brown bears congregate at Brooks Falls for the salmon run — 'unlike any other wildlife viewing experience we've ever had.' Getting there: commercial flight to King Salmon, then float plane or water taxi to Brooks Camp (or day tours from Anchorage, King Salmon, Homer or Seward). Camping permits release in January/February; the lodge runs on a lottery about 1.5 years out. Best late June through September, July best of all; allow 1-3 days; and everyone goes to 'bear school' on arrival.
additional_sources.source_title: Katmai — the national park for bear lovers

additional_sources.best_for: National park / The Dry Tortugas planning reel — ferry costs and warnings
additional_sources.recommendation: Their Dry Tortugas planning reel: the most remote national park on the East Coast, 70 miles off the coast of Key West, reached only by seaplane or boat. They took the ferry — tickets were $235 per person and must be booked at least a few months in advance as they sell out quickly; the 2.5-hour ride can be rough and is not recommended if you are prone to seasickness. On the island: explore Fort Jefferson, the largest brick masonry structure in the Western Hemisphere, walk the moat, and snorkel the abundant marine life and coral reefs (equipment included with the ticket). Pack an extra pair of dry clothes for the return trip.

additional_sources.best_for: Park guide / Their exact 3-day mini guide itinerary
additional_sources.recommendation: Their Rocky Mountain mini guide: Day 1 arrive via Denver, Lookout Mountain, the Peak to Peak Highway (Saint Catherine's Chapel on the Rock and Lily Lake), dinner and a stay in Estes Park. Day 2 the Bear Lake corridor lakes chain, Sprague Lake, Trail Ridge Road's overlooks and the Alpine Ridge Trail. Day 3 a strenuous hike (Sky Pond or Chasm Lake), Moraine Park, and the wildlife-rich western side to Grand Lake. Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road passes at 5 AM both days; Lookout Mountain, the chapel, Lily Lake and Moraine Park are named in the post but unpinned.

additional_sources.best_for: Park guide / Top tips — start early, go on weekdays, respect the altitude
additional_sources.recommendation: Their Rocky Mountain top tips from park #17: start as early as possible (Bear Lake corridor lots fill by 5:30 AM on summer weekends; there is a shuttle), visit on weekdays, drive Trail Ridge Road in summer, plan around the timed-entry reservation system, take altitude sickness seriously, bring bug spray and sun protection — and do not limit yourself to one area: the Bear Lake corridor, Trail Ridge Road and the quieter, wildlife-rich western side are all favorites.
additional_sources.source_title: Rocky Mountain landscapes are unreal — our top tips

additional_sources.best_for: Park guide / Rocky Mountain planning guide — timed entry, lodging, timing
additional_sources.recommendation: Their Rocky Mountain planning guide: stay in Estes Park or Grand Lake (Boulder and Loveland are about an hour away, Denver 1.5 hours), start as early as possible, summer is best because Trail Ridge Road is open (but it is also the busiest), allow 3+ days, take altitude sickness seriously, and never approach wildlife — they generally saw more on the quieter western side. The video adds the reservation mechanics: Timed Entry via recreation.gov (choose the 'Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road' option for full access), extra tickets released the night before at 7 PM MT, and Bear Lake corridor parking filling by 5:30 AM on a summer Saturday — use the shuttle.

places.name: Manitou Incline
places.best_for: Hike
places.recommendation: Joe Ferrucci and his friend Jordan set out to climb the Manitou Incline, billed on-screen as the tallest staircase in the United States. Jordan grinds his way up the relentless steps to the summit; Joe's own 'halfway through' update is filmed from a bar stool. A comedy bit, but an honest preview of how steep this climb is.
places.note: Geocoded as 'The Incline' (OSM, type: steps), Manitou Springs, El Paso County, CO.
places.source_title: Manitou Incline hike — 'Hold on I forgot something'

places.best_for: Fall colors / View
places.name: Eagle Tower
places.note: The reel says the views overlook Lake Michigan; the tower actually faces Green Bay (the bay between the Door Peninsula and mainland Wisconsin), with Horseshoe Island in view. Caption puts the park about a 5-hour drive from Chicago. The rebuilt tower (opened 2021) is reached by 95-100 stairs or an 850-foot accessible canopy ramp; Wisconsin DNR lists it open May 1-Oct 31.
places.recommendation: The reel's headline stop: add Peninsula State Park in Door County to a Wisconsin trip for Eagle Tower, reached by a long wooden elevated walkway through autumn trees to panoramic views over Green Bay and the surrounding islands — at their best in fall color. Parking, restrooms and park information are right at the tower area.
places.source_title: Fall colors — Eagle Tower, Peninsula State Park

additional_sources.best_for: Fall colors / View
additional_sources.recommendation: Asia's follow-up Peninsula State Park reel leads with Eagle Tower again: the elevated wooden boardwalk through peak autumn color out to the overlook above the water, pitched as the park's headline view on a Wisconsin trip about 5 hours from Chicago.
additional_sources.source_title: Peninsula State Park, Door County — a must-add Wisconsin trip

places.best_for: Hike
places.name: Eagle Trail
places.note: Pin is the Eagle Trail trailhead just west of the Eagle Tower parking area (Trailforks trailhead coordinates); DNR lists access at Eagle Terrace, Eagle Panorama or the Tower. DNR rates this 2.0-mile loop 'more difficult', with steep, rocky sections under 150-foot cliffs along Eagle Harbor.
places.recommendation: Shown in the reel right after the tower: the trailhead sign marked 'Difficult Trail' for the park's Eagle Trail, a loop the narrator points viewers to for more scenic overlooks beyond Eagle Tower.
places.source_title: Fall colors — Eagle Tower, Peninsula State Park

additional_sources.best_for: Hike
additional_sources.recommendation: The same reel shows the Eagle Trail trailhead sign (marked 'Difficult Trail') and points to the park's hiking trails as the way to explore beyond the tower.
additional_sources.source_title: Peninsula State Park, Door County — a must-add Wisconsin trip

places.name: Kayenta Falls
places.best_for: Waterfall
places.recommendation: One of Southern Utah's rarest sights, per Mikey Loveridge: the 1,000-foot red-rock cliffs of Hell Hole Canyon near Ivins run bone dry most days, but after heavy rain three ephemeral waterfalls — Kayenta Falls — pour straight down the cliff faces in a vertical flash flood. He photographed the canyon completely dry on Nov 1, 2026, and in full flow the next day after the rain kept coming.
places.note: Pin is approximate: the ephemeral falls are not a mapped feature, so it sits on Kayenta Wash at the mouth of Hell Hole Canyon, just northwest of the Kayenta community in Ivins (OpenStreetMap). The falls flow only after heavy rain.
places.source_title: Kayenta Falls — A Vertical Flash Flood

places.name: Colchuck Lake
places.best_for: Hike
places.recommendation: Their candidate for the most beautiful lake in the USA: Colchuck Lake in the Enchantments outside Leavenworth. It's a 9-mile out-and-back with 2,340 ft of elevation gain (moderate-hard) — and extremely popular despite the effort. Their summer tip: get there extremely early; they arrived around 5 AM and the parking lot was nearly full, with 50+ cars along the road by the time they hiked out.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: Most beautiful lake in the USA? — Colchuck Lake

additional_sources.best_for: Hike
additional_sources.recommendation: Jess's take on a trail that 'still manages to blow me away every time': the color of the water, the views of Dragontail Peak, and Aasgard Pass climbing into the Core Enchantments — 'worth every step.' 9 miles, about 2,400 ft of gain, and one hazard the other reel didn't mention: a very persistent mountain goat named Fred who disputes trail right-of-way.
additional_sources.source_title: Colchuck Lake — and a mountain goat named Fred

places.best_for: Stargazing
places.recommendation: Visit Dark Skies PA's pick for the best stargazing setup at Cherry Springs: the Overnight Astronomy Observation Field, with concrete telescope pads, electrical outlets and WiFi. The rules that keep it world-class: a permit/registration is required, arrive and set up before dark (vehicles then stay in the adjacent lot), red lights only — no white light — no campfires, and quiet hours from midnight to 9 AM.
places.note: Pin shares the Cherry Springs State Park coordinates; the observation field is inside the park.
places.source_title: Overnight Astronomy Observation Field — Cherry Springs State Park

places.name: Kanab Sand Caves (Moqui Caverns)
places.best_for: Hike
places.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #1: caves carved into Navajo sandstone in the 1970s to harvest sand for glassmaking — now a free, photogenic scramble right off Highway 89, about 1.2 miles round trip with parking by the highway. Her caution: the scramble up can get a little scary; don't be afraid to turn back.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

places.name: Toquerville Falls
places.best_for: Waterfall
places.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #3: no hiking required if you have a 4x4 (don't attempt it in a normal car) — a 5.3-mile dirt road, about 45 minutes, to falls that pour over two pour-offs on La Verkin Creek: a cascade section and a clean 20-foot drop into a pool. Free BLM land, and the swimming is incredible in summer.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

places.name: Kanarra Falls
places.best_for: Waterfall
places.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #4 — her favorite of the five: a permitted slot-canyon waterfall hike, about 3.8 miles out and back with creek crossings the whole way and a ladder climb in the canyon. Permits sell out 1–2 weeks ahead in summer, so book early — and rent the waders unless you want numb feet for an hour afterwards.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

places.name: Water Canyon
places.best_for: Hike
places.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #5: a 4.25-mile out-and-back hike (about 500 ft of gain) that ends up looking like a mini version of Zion's Subway — and a pretty easy one. This is the one she says legit looks like the Subway.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

places.name: Red Slot Canyon (Red Hollow)
places.best_for: Slot canyon
places.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #2: a 1.2-mile round-trip slot canyon with glowing orange and pink walls. Park at the water facility at the end of Red Hollow Drive — and note the sandy road is popular with off-roaders, so it can be soft going.
places.note: The reel calls it 'Red Slot Canyon in Kanab' but its own access detail — park at the water facility at the end of Red Hollow Drive — identifies it as Red Hollow Slot Canyon near Orderville. Pin is the trailhead by the water tank; coordinates from two independent trail guides (37.2709, -112.6273), not OpenStreetMap.

places.site: Bentonite Hills (Cow Dung Road, near the Mars Desert Research Station)
places.best_for: Viewpoint

places.note: Two Bentonite Hills areas exist: the official ones inside Capitol Reef (Cathedral Valley) and the photographed BLM hills on Cow Dung Road near the Mars Desert Research Station outside Hanksville. Both source reels point to the Hanksville/MDRS hills (the 'none in a national park' list rules out the park site), so the pin uses the Cow Dung Road coordinates given by several independent guides (~38.4123, -110.7859).
places.source_title: 9 Places in Utah That Look Unreal — None in a National Park

additional_sources.best_for: Viewpoint
additional_sources.recommendation: Megs and Pat's Mars-on-Earth pick: hills of bentonite clay near Hanksville, just outside Capitol Reef, striped purple, pink, red, orange, grey and blue-green from volcanic ash and minerals. Their practical notes: on the road toward the Mars Desert Research Station; unpaved access, high-clearance 4WD recommended; best at sunrise or sunset when low light brings out the colours; and never after rain — wet bentonite turns extremely slippery and sticky and vehicles get stuck.
additional_sources.source_title: Bentonite Hills — a landscape from another planet

additional_sources.recommendation: Their Horseshoe Bend verdict: 'THIS MAY BE CONTROVERSIAL BUT DON'T GO TO HORSESHOE BEND AT SUNRISE' — the surrounding area lights up beautifully, but the canyon itself stays dark and shadowed, the wait for the light is long, and the viewpoint is crowded and overwhelming even then. They left and returned later the same day in full sun, when the bend was beautiful. Their recommendation: visit during the day or at sunset. The walk is an easy 1.5 miles round trip, and parking costs $10 regardless of an America the Beautiful Pass (they misspoke '$20' in the video and corrected it in the caption and comments). Worth visiting — just not their favorite stop of the road trip.

Non-technical (no special gear or skills), with a few steep rock-scramble sections. Their tips: pack plenty of water (few places to filter), no backpacking on the peak itself, and Thornton Lakes backpacking is by competitive NPS permit.

places.name: Million Dollar Highway (US-550)
places.best_for: Scenic drive
places.recommendation: American Travel Archives' 'you will NOT believe this road' drive: the Million Dollar Highway (US-550) from Ouray to Silverton — 25 miles through the San Juan Mountains famous for steep cliffs, tight switchbacks and few guardrails. Stop at Red Mountain Pass for the classic overlook; autumn is the best time, when golden aspens contrast with the red and gray rock. Their tips: drive it in good morning light, take your time at the pull-offs, and think twice in an RV. Ouray and Silverton bookend it with hot springs and silver-mining history.
places.note: Pin is at Red Mountain Pass, the highway's classic overlook (OpenStreetMap).

places.name: Snow Lake (Alpine Lakes)
places.best_for: Hike
places.recommendation: The Trekking Mama's 'how is this real?' lake: Snow Lake looks like it should require a plane ticket or a major expedition, but the trailhead is only about 60 minutes from Seattle. The water is an unbelievable bright alpine blue that looks photoshopped but isn't. It's popular and you'll share the trail — her tip is to keep going past the first viewpoints down toward the end of the lake, where the crowds thin out. Her go-to when someone visits Washington and needs a massive dose of alpine gorgeousness without planning a whole trip.
places.note: The Alpine Lakes Wilderness Snow Lake near Snoqualmie Pass — a different lake from the Snow Lake in Mount Rainier National Park, which is a separate pin. Pin is OpenStreetMap's named point for the lake.

additional_sources.best_for: Alpine lake / Hike · Turquoise water below Snoqualmie Pass peaks
additional_sources.recommendation: Nicole's take: Snow Lake is a stunning alpine lake hike just off I-90 near Snoqualmie Pass, only 45 min from Seattle — beautiful mountain views and crystal-clear turquoise water that looks almost unreal. Her card: 7.2 miles round trip, ~1,800 ft of gain, NW Forest Pass or America the Beautiful at the trailhead, and if you want to extend the adventure, continue on to Gem Lake. Leave no trace.
additional_sources.source_title: Snow Lake — a stunning alpine lake just 45 min from Seattle

additional_sources.best_for: Viewpoint

The hike is 1.5 miles round trip with about 200 ft of gain: forest trails, boardwalks, stairs and multiple ocean viewpoints. A Makah Recreation Permit is required (online or in Neah Bay before the trailhead); open daily from dawn until 30 minutes after sunset, year-round. Her tips: it's a remote drive with spotty cell service, so download directions ahead, bring a rain jacket, and stay on the designated trails and viewing platforms.

places.name: Alvord Desert
places.best_for: Stargazing
places.recommendation: Jess drove 9 hours to camp on the Alvord Desert playa — under some of the darkest skies in Oregon — to teach herself astrophotography. She timed the trip under an almost-full moon by accident, so she waited for moonset, set a 3:24 AM alarm, and manually shot 105 long exposures (her old Sony has no intervalometer) to stitch a four-second starlapse. Her verdict: the Alvord had been on her list a long time and was worth every bit of the drive.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: Alvord Desert — a 3:24 AM starlapse on the playa

places.name: Whipple's Cave
places.best_for: Hike
places.recommendation: A cave hiding in the Illinois woods: Whipple's Cave in Franklin Creek State Natural Area, reached via the Pioneer Pass Trail from the Mill Springs Day Use Area — 2.9 miles out and back with 226 ft of gain through wooded scenery, rocky terrain and creek crossings. Know before you go: be prepared for deep creek crossings, and other trails in the area also lead to the cave.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: Whipple's Cave — a cave hiding in the Illinois woods

places.name: Mount Si
places.site: Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area
places.best_for: Hike
places.recommendation: WTA calls Mount Si the most popular hike in Washington — upwards of 100,000 hikers a year. The switchbacks start right at the trailhead; a mile and a half up you pass through Snag Flat, old-growth trees that survived fire and logging, then past a talus slope to the base of the Haystack, the true summit. 8.0 miles round trip with 3,150 ft of gain. Climbers training for Rainier haul heavy packs up here — the rule of thumb is that if you can make the top in under two hours, you're ready. A Discover Pass is required to park, and the lot fills early.
places.note: Coordinates verified against OpenStreetMap.
places.source_title: Mount Si — Washington's most popular hike

places.name: Wolf Creek Falls
places.best_for: Waterfall
places.recommendation: Amory's #5 unique national park waterfall: Wolf Creek Falls in New River Gorge — a wide, moss-covered cascade where water seeps and sheets over rocks beside the hiking trail.
places.note: Approximate pin — it sits on Wolf Creek by Fayette Station Road (the USGS place-name point for the creek); the falls itself is not a separately mapped feature.
places.source_title: Top 5 Unique National Park Waterfalls

places.name: Cataract Falls (Kenai Fjords)
places.best_for: Waterfall
places.recommendation: Amory's #2 unique national park waterfall: Cataract Falls in Kenai Fjords — massive waterfalls pouring down sheer coastal cliffs directly into the ocean, seen from a boat.
places.note: Pin is at Cataract Cove in the Northwestern Fjord (OpenStreetMap) — the boat-tour stop named for its waterfalls, where the falls pour down the cove's cliffs into the sea.
places.source_title: Top 5 Unique National Park Waterfalls

places.name: Princess Arch
places.best_for: Hike
places.recommendation: A 1/4-mile walk on Princess Arch Trail (#233) to Princess Arch, a natural sandstone arch in Red River Gorge — the reel hikes it at peak fall color, with a sandstone ledge overlook above a valley of red and gold trees on the way.
places.note: Coordinates from OpenStreetMap's named Princess Arch point on Trail #233 (Wolfe County side of the gorge). Red River Gorge is in Daniel Boone National Forest; the creator's caption points to her series of 5+ Red River Gorge videos.
places.source_title: Princess Arch Trail in fall — Red River Gorge

places.name: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park
places.best_for: Swimming
places.recommendation: One of the most unique swims in the Midwest: hundreds of natural pools and chutes the Black River carved into billion-year-old volcanic rock — 'nature's own waterpark,' about 2 hours south of St. Louis. The reel's tips: go early in summer (it gets busy), wear water shoes for the slippery rock, and mind the stronger currents with kids.
places.note: Pin sits at the main shut-ins day-use area (OpenStreetMap point for the swimming area's supply store) rather than the park boundary centroid. The 'shut-ins' are narrow channels where the river squeezes through erosion-resistant rhyolite.
places.source_title: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park — nature's waterpark in Missouri

places.name: Wyalusing State Park
places.best_for: Caves / Stargazing
places.recommendation: 'This state park surprised us': 14+ miles of trails with caves to explore, an astronomy center that's perfect for stargazing, and four campgrounds on the bluffs near Bagley. Day pass $13 in-state / $16 out-of-state, per the reel.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's Wyalusing State Park point. The reel does not name the cave it films (stairs up a cliffside into a sandy-floored cave with lookout openings), so no cave name is recorded.
places.source_title: This state park surprised us — Wyalusing State Park, Wisconsin

places.name: Old Immigrant & Bluff Loop
places.best_for: Hike
places.recommendation: The creators' favorite trail in the park: the Old Immigrant & Bluff Loop — the hike the reel films, past a natural-arch rock formation and up wooden stairs built against the cliff to a cave with sandy floors, crawl spaces, and openings that look out over the forest.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's Old Immigrant Trail point within Wyalusing State Park.
places.source_title: This state park surprised us — Wyalusing State Park, Wisconsin

places.name: Hawk Hill
places.best_for: Viewpoint
places.recommendation: It looks like Hawaii's Stairway to Heaven, but it's just north of San Francisco: an easy climb of about 650 steps from the parking area to panoramic views — the Pacific on one side, the Golden Gate Bridge on the other. No long hike, free parking off Conzelman Road.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's Hawk Hill peak point on Conzelman Road in the Marin Headlands (Golden Gate National Recreation Area); the reel's listed address is Hawk Hill, Conzelman Rd, Sausalito, CA 94965.
places.source_title: Hawk Hill — a 'Stairway to Heaven' viewpoint over the Golden Gate

places.name: Big Sur (Highway 1)
places.best_for: Scenic drive
places.recommendation: One of the five, and the caption's headliner: Big Sur — Highway 1 along green grassy cliffs above the Pacific and its rocky shoreline, the most famous coastal drive in California.
places.note: Pin at Bixby Creek Bridge (OpenStreetMap), the iconic span on the Big Sur stretch of Highway 1.

places.name: Seven Teacups
places.best_for: Waterfall
places.recommendation: A surreal chain of smooth white-granite pools on Dry Meadow Creek, each cup dropping 6 to 20 feet into the next before the water slides into the Kern River. Reached by a roughly 4-mile round-trip hike with about 850 feet of gain, rock scrambling and a creek crossing. The creator's warning, kept verbatim in spirit: please don't swim — the current can pull swimmers under even when the water looks calm.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's Seven Teacups waterfall point near Johnsondale Bridge, under 2 hours from Bakersfield. The reel names the AllTrails route 'Seven Tea Cups Viewpoint via Dry Creek Meadow' and mentions Johnny McNally's Fairview Lodge-Restaurant, about 10 minutes away, as a nearby stop (an amenity mention, not pinned).
places.source_title: Seven Teacups — granite pools above the Kern River

places.name: Torch Lake
places.best_for: Fall colors
places.recommendation: The 'Caribbean of the Midwest' in autumn: Torch Lake's turquoise, crystal-clear water and shallow sandbars ringed by peak fall color — the reel's drone shots show deep blue open water against shores of red and gold. The caption pitches the area's wineries and orchards as a perfect Michigan fall road trip.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's point for the long Torch Lake near Traverse City (Antrim County) — not the smaller Torch Lake in the Keweenaw Peninsula.
places.source_title: Torch Lake in Fall feels like the movies

places.name: Cape Kiwanda
places.best_for: Hike · Sand dune climb, tide pools and coastal views
places.recommendation: Climb the 240-foot sand dune for the payoff view over sandstone cliffs, tide pools and sandy beaches, with Pacific City's own Haystack Rock offshore. There's also an easier 1-mile walk along the beach to the rocks of the cape.
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's point for the Cape Kiwanda headland.
places.source_title: Cape Kiwanda — 12/10 view on the Oregon Coast

places.name: Penn's Cave
places.best_for: Cave tour · America's only all-water cavern, toured by boat
places.recommendation: The reel's first stop: a boat ride through America's only all-water cavern — you float the underground river past illuminated stalactites instead of walking. It's also the only Pennsylvania cave on the National Register of Historic Places, with a wildlife park above ground.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2
places.note: Coordinates from the venue's published location, 222 Penns Cave Rd, Centre Hall (OpenStreetMap has no attraction point for the cave).

places.name: Bilger's Rocks
places.best_for: Hike · Ancient sandstone rock maze
places.recommendation: A 300-million-year-old sandstone 'rock city' in Clearfield County — moss-covered boulders split into narrow passageways and small caves; the reel's presenter squeezes through the crevices and wanders the forest among the rocks.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2

places.name: Benezette Elk Viewing
places.best_for: Wildlife · Wild elk herd viewing
places.recommendation: The reel stops in Elk County near Benezette for Pennsylvania's wild elk herd — wide fields at sunrise and sunset and a big bull elk filmed from the roadside. The Elk Country Visitor Center on Winslow Hill is the hub of the viewing area.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2
places.note: Pin is the Elk Country Visitor Center in Benezette, the center of the Winslow Hill elk-viewing area the reel films.

places.name: Pine Creek Gorge (PA Grand Canyon)
places.best_for: Scenic overlook · PA Grand Canyon overlooks and Turkey Path waterfall
places.recommendation: Tioga County's 'Grand Canyon of Pennsylvania' — a roughly 45-mile-long, 1,000-foot-deep forested gorge. The reel shows the rim overlooks at Leonard Harrison State Park, hikers on the cliff edges, and the Turkey Path trail dropping past its waterfall toward Pine Creek.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2

places.name: Wellsboro
places.best_for: Small town stop · Gas-lit Main Street and the Wellsboro Diner
places.recommendation: The reel's small-town stop: Wellsboro's historic, gas-lit Main Street, its storefronts and the classic Wellsboro Diner — the gateway town for the Pine Creek Gorge.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2

places.name: Austin Dam Ruins
places.best_for: Historic site · Ruins of the 1911 Austin Dam failure
places.recommendation: Honorable mention in the reel's caption: the towering concrete ruins of the Austin Dam in Potter County, which failed in 1911 and destroyed the town below — now a memorial park.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2
places.note: Pin is OpenStreetMap's Austin Dam Overlook viewpoint.

places.name: Kinzua Bridge State Park

places.recommendation: Honorable mention in the reel's caption: the Kinzua Viaduct in McKean County — once among the longest and highest railroad bridges in the world, toppled by a tornado in 2003 and reinvented as a skywalk out over the gorge, with the twisted towers still lying in the valley below.
places.source_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2
places.note: The skywalk has been under intermittent repair closures scheduled through 2027, with seasonal openings — check the park page before going.

places.name: Cucumber Falls
places.best_for: Waterfall · 36-foot falls you can walk behind, on a 5-minute trail
places.recommendation: A beautiful waterfall you can stand inside of: a 36-foot bridal-veil falls on the Great Gorge Trail in Ohiopyle State Park, reached by a very short, super-maintained trail — under five minutes, with a scenic overlook at the start — that the creator stresses is easy enough for kids and elderly visitors. Scramble over the rocks at the base and you can walk behind the curtain of water.
places.source_title: Cucumber Falls — the waterfall you can stand inside

places.name: Massacre Rim

places.source_title: You haven't really seen the night sky until you've visited places like these

places.name: Big Bend Ranch State Park
places.best_for: Stargazing · Vast desert with minimal light pollution

places.source_title: You haven't really seen the night sky until you've visited places like these

places.name: Homestead Crater
places.best_for: Hot spring · Swim inside a 55-foot limestone crater
places.recommendation: A hidden underground hot spring inside a 55-foot-tall limestone crater: a naturally heated geothermal pool at 90–96°F year-round, about 65 feet deep, that you can soak, swim, snorkel or even scuba dive in. It's at the Homestead Resort in Midway, just outside Park City, but day visitors are welcome — $30 per person (the reel notes it was $15 when filmed) for a 60-minute session with about 40 minutes in the water; life jackets are required and provided, and reservations are recommended since weekends fill up.
places.source_title: There's a hidden underground hot spring in Utah… and you can swim inside it!

places.recommendation: A whole underground world near Madison: colorful rock formations, sparkling crystals and winding passages on guided tours offered year-round. The cave holds a steady 50°F, so bring a light jacket; it's a great family-friendly stop even on a rainy day, and the grounds above ground are worth exploring too.

places.recommendation: Two rare meromictic lakes — Green Lake and Round Lake — whose deep waters never mix seasonally, and whose unusual chemistry creates a striking blue-green color that looks like it should need a passport. Walk the easy shoreline trail, swim at the beach in season, kayak, or picnic — a few hours of exploring without needing a major hike.
places.source_title: I thought this shade of blue required a passport

places.name: Needles Eye Tunnel
places.best_for: Scenic drive · One-lane tunnel carved through granite
places.recommendation: The Needles Highway through Custer State Park winds between towering granite spires until the road tightens and passes through the Needles Eye Tunnel — a one-lane tunnel hand-carved through solid granite in the 1920s, one of the most photographed drives in the Black Hills. Know before you go: the tunnel is about 8'4" wide and 12' tall, one vehicle at a time, and RVs/trailers should avoid the route; drive it early morning or late afternoon for fewer cars and better light, and watch for bison, pronghorn and prairie dogs nearby.
places.source_title: This state park drive feels unreal the first time you see it

places.name: Quarry Exhibit Hall
places.best_for: Fossils · A building built around a wall of dinosaur bones
places.recommendation: About 30 minutes east of Vernal, a shuttle takes you to the Quarry Exhibit Hall — a building constructed around the sloped rock face where a 'log jam' of dinosaur bones was found in 1909. Hundreds of thousands of bones were excavated for museums around the world, but the rest were left in place, so you can see — and touch — real fossils where they were buried. You can shuttle back or hike back down for more fossils in the rock formations. The monument spans Utah and Colorado; the quarry is on the Utah side, and the creators wished they'd had time for more trails and a Green River float.
places.source_title: Finding, seeing, touching dinosaur fossils at Dinosaur National Monument

places.name: Rainbow Springs State Park
places.best_for: Spring swimming · Kayak a crystal-clear 72°F river
places.recommendation: One of the oldest and most beautiful spring-fed rivers in Florida: crystal-clear water at 72°F year-round, surrounded by lush greenery that feels like a tropical jungle. It's Florida's 4th-largest spring; the headspring area was a privately owned theme park in the 1930s. Kayak, paddleboard, swim in the designated area, or walk the garden trails to see waterfalls — real ones, in Florida. Open daily 8 AM to sunset, $2 entry (tubing and kayak rentals extra). Pro tip from the reel: come early morning or late afternoon to beat the crowds, and bring your own snorkel gear to spot fish and turtles.
places.source_title: Rainbow Springs — Florida's crystal-clear spring river

places.name: Weston Bend State Park
places.best_for: Scenic overlook · Fall hiking above the Missouri River
places.recommendation: The reel's day-trip anchor, 40 minutes from Kansas City: start at the scenic overlook for sweeping views of the Missouri River valley and fall foliage, then walk the wooded bluff trails (paved and natural-surface options). There's a campground too — the creators camped here and recommend it for turning the day trip into a weekend.
places.source_title: A fall day trip 40 minutes from Kansas City: Weston Bend + Weston, MO

places.name: Weston
places.best_for: Small town · Historic downtown, shops and fall orchards
places.recommendation: The reel's second stop: downtown Weston, with adorable local shops, boutiques and historic streets — plus nearby orchards, seasonal farm activities, and fall events to round out the day trip.
places.source_title: A fall day trip 40 minutes from Kansas City: Weston Bend + Weston, MO

places.name: Kitch-iti-kipi
places.best_for: Spring · Self-propelled raft over turquoise water
places.recommendation: Michigan's largest freshwater spring, inside Palms Book State Park: turquoise water so crystal clear you can see straight to the bottom, at a constant 45°F, viewed from a self-propelled wooden observation raft you crank across the spring yourself. Open year-round; a Michigan Recreation Passport (state park pass) is required. No swimming or fishing, but it's pet friendly and ADA accessible.
places.source_title: Kitch-iti-kipi — Michigan's crystal-clear Big Spring

additional_sources.best_for: Spring · Turquoise big spring on a self-propelled raft
additional_sources.recommendation: Also on this Michigan fall itinerary: Kitch-iti-kipi shown from the wooden viewing platform/raft — the bright turquoise spring with other visitors taking in the crystal-clear water.
additional_sources.source_title: Michigan fall itinerary — no mountains, so waterfalls

places.name: Mount Mitchell
places.best_for: Summit · Highest peak in the eastern US (6,684 ft)
places.recommendation: At 6,684 feet, Mount Mitchell is the highest peak in the eastern United States — the highest point east of the Mississippi. The reel puts it on the North Carolina bucket list for the sweeping Blue Ridge Mountain views that make the drive up (off the Blue Ridge Parkway, near Asheville) worth it.
places.source_title: The highest point east of the Mississippi
places.source_reel_theme: North Carolina / Blue Ridge bucket list
places.note: Pin is the summit (Nominatim peak point).

places.name: Goat Trail to Big Bluff
places.best_for: Hike · Narrow ledge trail on a 550-ft bluff over the Buffalo River
places.recommendation: A strenuous 6-mile round trip in the Ponca Wilderness: follow the Centerpoint Trail down from Highway 43, then take the Goat Trail spur — a narrow ledge carved across the face of Big Bluff, at 550 feet one of the tallest sheer bluffs between the Rockies and the Appalachians — for the huge view over the Buffalo River. Rugged, rocky, and a real climb back out; the reel's trail warning is plenty of horse poop along the way. Not for kids or anyone afraid of heights.
places.source_title: You hiked 6 miles to see THIS Arkansas view
places.note: Pin is the Centerpoint Trailhead on AR-43 north of Ponca (the hike's start); Big Bluff is about 3 trail-miles in.

places.name: Hemmed-In Hollow Falls
places.best_for: Waterfall / Hike · Tallest waterfall between the Rockies and Appalachians
places.recommendation: A nearly 210-foot waterfall hidden in the Ponca Wilderness of Buffalo National River — the tallest waterfall between the Rocky and Appalachian Mountains. The journey is part of it: a steep, rugged hike drops nearly 1,400 feet into the hollow, and you climb every bit of it back out. Key catch from the reel: it's rain-fed, so it can be a powerful cascade after significant rainfall or barely a trickle in dry periods — go after rain (late winter through spring is peak flow).
places.source_title: Arkansas is keeping too many secrets — a nearly 210-foot waterfall

places.name: Pinnacles Youth Park
places.best_for: Hike · Towering rock pinnacles and fossil hunting
places.recommendation: One of the most unique places in Missouri: a privately owned park north of Columbia (850 E. Pinnacles Rd, Sturgeon) that's open for public day use and feels like a rugged hike out west. Lower trails run along the creek to a shelter bluff for all ages; the real adventure is crossing the creek and taking the narrow, rocky path over the top of the towering rock formations. The spot is full of fossils — look in the creek and across the rocks for thousands of crinoids. Free (donation box at the kiosk); vault restroom; no alcohol, glass or drones. The reel's warnings: the upper ledge trails are not for young kids or anyone afraid of heights, don't cross the creek when the water is high, and expect wet feet even in summer.
places.source_title: This is Missouri?! Pinnacles Youth Park

additional_sources.best_for: Hike · Towering rock pinnacles and fossil hunting
additional_sources.recommendation: Also a stop on this Columbia + Rocheport fall day trip: a hidden gem that's private property but open to the public — lower trails to a shelter cave and creek for all ages, while older kids and adults can carefully climb along the rock Pinnacles. places.name: Homans Path
places.best_for: Hike · Short historic stone-step path to Dorr Mountain
places.recommendation: One of the shortest hikes in Acadia National Park might also be one of the most unique: tucked into the Sieur de Monts area near Bar Harbor, Homans Path is just 0.3 miles one way (0.8 mi out-and-back with ~334 ft of climb) but packs in intricate granite staircases, narrow forest passages, historic stonework, a stone 'hallway' and beautiful views on a short but steep climb. The reel pairs it into a half-day Sieur de Monts itinerary: Wild Gardens of Acadia, the Nature Center, the Jesup Path boardwalk, then Homans Path, with the Island Explorer shuttle as an option. The path is a memorial trail honoring Eliza Lothrop Homans' land donations; it joins the Schiff Path toward the summit of Dorr Mountain.
places.source_title: One of the shortest hikes in Acadia might be the most unique: Homans Path
places.note: Pin is Sieur de Monts Spring — the trail begins at Sieur de Monts, steps from the spring and the Wild Gardens of Acadia.

places.name: Crimson Canyon
places.best_for: Slot canyon / Guided tour · Antelope-style canyon without the crowds
places.recommendation: The reel's pitch: people pay hundreds to visit Antelope Canyon, but almost no one knows about this slot canyon near Zion — towering red sandstone walls (100+ ft high, 6–10 ft wide), winding passageways and incredible photo opportunities WITHOUT the crowds. The catch, stated honestly in the reel: Crimson Canyon itself has no entrance fee, but you can't access it independently because the route crosses private property — you book a guided tour with a company that has permission. They booked East Zion Adventures and loved it: a ~2-hour trip, UTV ride into the backcountry from Orderville, then a guided hike with short climbs (obstacles up to ~10 ft).
places.source_title: People pay hundreds for Antelope Canyon — almost no one knows this slot canyon near Zion
places.note: Pin is the tour meeting point in Orderville (15 E State St — check-in at the Sinclair station coffee shop, per East Zion Adventures' listings); the canyon itself is on private land reached by UTV and has no public coordinates.

places.name: Mount Monadnock
places.best_for: Hike / Summit · Bare rocky summit with 360° views
places.recommendation: Calvin's reel takes on Mt. Monadnock in southern New Hampshire — the 3,165-ft peak that gave 'monadnock' its name (an isolated mountain rising from the plain), reputed to be one of the most-climbed mountains in the world. The classic route is the White Dot Trail up from the state park headquarters (3.4–3.6 mi round trip, ~1,750 ft gain, with rock scrambles and stone steps) and down the White Cross — the bare, rocky summit opens to sweeping views across southern New Hampshire and, on clear days, all six New England states. A National Natural Landmark with a literary streak: Emerson and Thoreau both climbed and wrote about it. No dogs allowed on the mountain.
places.source_title: Mt. Monadnock in New Hampshire

The reel's tips: hike the loop clockwise, parking at the South Falls lot to start; bring a credit card ($5 parking at some lots, machines on site); expect to get a little wet walking behind the falls, so bring a rain jacket in colder months; grab the park trail map or an app like AllTrails first, since one or two falls need a side trail; dogs can't hike this trail (take them on the Rim Trail instead); and start early — it's popular.

Trail volunteers have rerouted and marked the path with cairns and ribbons — stick to the defined trail and download offline maps to navigate.

places.name: Devil's Bathtub
places.site: Devil's Fork Loop Trail / Jefferson National Forest
places.best_for: Swimming hole / Hike · Emerald rock pool down 13 creek crossings
places.recommendation: 13 creek crossings to reach a bathtub the creek carved for itself: Devil's Bathtub near Fort Blackmore, VA (Scott County, ~30 min from Natural Tunnel) — emerald water swirling through a smooth rock pool, and the name is backed by ~65°F water even in July. The reel's practical card: the Devil's Fork Trail is ~4 mi round trip with 13 unbridged crossings (or a 7-mi no-crossing route), budget 3–5 hours and 3 PM as the last start; don't go if the water is above your knees — the holler flash floods; free lot at 312 High Knob SC, Dungannon VA (no roadside parking — towed); go weekdays or early. Swimming season is over by fall — the hike is the experience then.
places.source_title: Devil's Bathtub, Virginia — 13 creek crossings to a rock-carved bathtub
places.note: Pin is the OSM attraction point for Devil's Bathtub itself.

places.name: Marshall's Beach
places.site: Golden Gate National Recreation Area / Presidio
places.best_for: Beach / Viewpoint · Golden Gate views without the crowds
places.recommendation: San Francisco's most underrated Golden Gate view — and you'll probably have it to yourself. The family's route: park at the Langdon Court lot (free, mostly empty around 10 AM), walk toward Battery West, then take the Batteries to Bluffs Trail down to the beach (~0.5 mile, stairs involved — their 4- and 5-year-olds handled it fine), turn right toward Marshall's Beach and down a few more stairs. They stayed almost an hour without seeing another person. Safety notes from the reel: don't go at high tide — the beach becomes mostly inaccessible and dangerous, so check tides first; no restrooms or facilities; and it's a clothing-optional beach, worth knowing if you're bringing kids.
places.source_title: Marshall's Beach — San Francisco's most underrated Golden Gate view
places.note: Pin is the OSM beach point for Marshall's Beach, below the Batteries to Bluffs Trail.

places.name: Devil's Den Prehistoric Spring
places.best_for: Swimming / Snorkel & dive · Underground spring inside a dry cave
places.recommendation: Episode 1 of Jete's American Bucket List: Devil's Den in Williston, Florida (5390 NE 180th Ave) — you can swim inside the earth. It's an underground spring in a dry cave, over 100 feet across, reached only by descending a staircase into the sinkhole; it got its name because people once saw 'smoke' (winter steam) rising from the hole and thought it was where the devil lives. The water is 72°F year-round and you can snorkel or scuba dive — the reel's headline price was $30. Animal fossils from millions of years ago (Pleistocene finds, now at the UF Museum of Natural History) have been found down there.
places.source_title: Devil's Den, Florida — swim inside the earth for $30 (American Bucket List ep. 1)
places.note: Coordinates are the published Devil's Den Cave point (Wikipedia); the business's own listing puts it at the same spot (±0.001°). The Dyrt's printed coordinates (29.439, -82.530) are wrong and were rejected.

places.name: Royal Gorge Route Railroad
places.best_for: Scenic train / Canyon views · 1,000-ft gorge from an open-air car
places.recommendation: Insane canyon views without hiking or driving sketchy roads: the Royal Gorge Route Railroad out of Cañon City, Colorado (~1 hr from Colorado Springs). The train runs the Arkansas River through a 1,000+ ft deep canyon with sheer granite cliffs on both sides, passing under the famous Royal Gorge Bridge — bald eagles, rafters, and dramatic rock formations along the route, with the best photo ops from the open-air car. Know before you go, per the reel: the ride is about 2 hours roundtrip and slow by design (scenery, not speed); parking is easy near the depot; there's a full kitchen and bar on most departures; and you can pair it with Royal Gorge Bridge Park if you have extra time.
places.source_title: Royal Gorge Route Railroad — insane canyon views, no hiking required
places.note: Pin is the OSM station point for the Royal Gorge Route Railroad depot in Cañon City, where the ride boards.

places.name: Vesper Peak
places.site: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mountain Loop Highway)
places.best_for: Summit hike / Sunset · Steep alpine climb to a 6,214-ft summit
places.recommendation: Sunset on Vesper Peak — one of the most rewarding hikes off Washington's Mountain Loop Highway. The reel's card: about 6.5 miles round trip with 4,120 ft of gain; plan 6–8 hours (their hike took 5h40, and it runs longer than it looks — preparation is key, carry the 10 essentials). The trail starts in forest with steady switchbacks, then opens to alpine meadows, rocky slopes and big views; Vesper Lake near the top is a beautiful break spot (filter any water); the last stretch is steep and rocky. Sunset tip: start early enough to be at the summit before golden hour and bring a headlamp for the hike down. Pack layers, extra water, and traction in early season (snow can linger into summer); a Northwest Forest Pass is needed at the trailhead.
places.source_title: Sunset on Vesper Peak — one of the most rewarding hikes off the Mountain Loop Highway
places.note: Pin is the OSM summit point for Vesper Peak (6,214 ft); the hike starts at the Sunrise Mine trailhead off the Mountain Loop Highway.

places.name: Green River Gorge Resort
places.best_for: Waterfall / Hidden gem · Walk behind a waterfall into a cave
places.recommendation: Don't miss this hidden gem: the Green River Gorge Resort property near Enumclaw, WA. The resort dates to the 1920s, when it operated as a privately owned getaway with a hotel and cabins; by the 1970s and '80s it had become a well-known local party spot. The resort itself no longer operates, but the property and trails are still accessible — check out the bridge, walk behind a waterfall into a hidden cave, and explore the area's unique rock formations. The reel's practical notes: $5 for parking, paid at a cash box; no restrooms; and the trail can be slippery, so watch your step. Leave no trace.
places.source_title: Green River Gorge Resort — a hidden gem with a waterfall cave near Enumclaw
places.note: Pin is the published Green River Gorge Resort point (29500 SE Green River Gorge Rd, Enumclaw) — the trail access for the gorge, bridge, and waterfall cave.

places.name: Beckham Creek Cave Lodge
places.best_for: Stay / Unique stay · Sleep inside a living cave in the Ozarks
places.recommendation: Would you stay the night in this cave? Buried in the Ozark Mountains, Beckham Creek Cave Lodge (@beckhamcave) in Parthenon, Arkansas was once a private Cold War fallout shelter and has since been converted into one of the most beautiful and unique homes in the world. The 5,800 sq ft cave has 4 bedrooms, each with its own bathroom, and comfortably sleeps up to 12 guests — for less than $300 a person per night with a group. It was featured on Netflix's “World's Most Amazing Vacation Rentals,” and they offer cave tours you can take without staying the night.
places.source_title: Would you stay the night in this cave? Beckham Creek Cave Lodge
places.note: Pin is the lodge's published point (1110 NC 8641, Parthenon, AR 72666) — the business listing, the Newton County Chamber's map embed, and showcaves.com all agree within ~150 ft.

places.name: Cascades Falls
places.best_for: Waterfall / 66-foot waterfall at the end of a creekside climb
places.recommendation: One of the best hikes in Virginia, and the waterfall is incredible: Cascades Falls in Pembroke, Virginia — she hiked it with her 8-year-old. It's 2 miles out and 2 miles back plus lots of elevation gain — a hard hike for beginners, but doable with kids (not recommended for kids under 6). About 4 hours from northern Virginia and 3 hours from Richmond. Her tips for solo moms and solo adventurers: bring way more water than you think you'll need and be prepared to take many breaks. (The falls themselves are a 66-foot cascade on Little Stony Creek, reached by the Cascades National Recreation Trail — US Forest Service.)
places.source_title: Cascades Falls, Pembroke Virginia — one of the best hikes in Virginia
places.note: Pin is the falls themselves on Little Stony Creek (published waterfall GPS; trail guides and the Forest Service agree). The Cascades Day Use Area trailhead/parking is ~1.5 mi southwest at 37.35301, -80.59984 (2068 Cascade Dr, $3/car day-use fee).

Best time to visit is fall through spring; plan one full day; park hours are 7 AM to sunset and the gate is closed outside them; bring lots of water, snacks and sun protection; nearby missile testing sometimes closes the park. places.name: Mooney Falls
places.best_for: Waterfall / Nearly 200-foot falls reached by a chain-and-ladder cliff descent
places.recommendation: Episode 5 of Cassie Compton's (@lafftravel) 'hikes to do before your knees give out': Mooney Falls drops nearly 200 feet into the most ridiculously blue water she's ever seen — but reaching the base means climbing down a cliff on chains, ladders and footholds carved into the rock. It's part of the Havasupai backpacking trip (10 miles in with a 35-pound pack on her first-ever backpacking trip; she lost three toenails and would do it all again in a heartbeat). A Havasupai reservation and permit are required, and the descent is steep and slippery — definitely not for everyone, but unforgettable if you're comfortable with heights.
